dedupe_keys.name: cpas the uk s national machine learning hospital capacity planning system for covid 19

description: This case study describes the COVID-19 Capacity Planning and Analysis System, a machine learning decision support system that forecast demand for hospital resources, especially intensive care, and was deployed at individual hospitals and across regions of the UK in coordination with NHS Digital. The authors, from the University of Cambridge, published it as a preprint. The paper sets out the challenges of deploying such a system nationally and how the system met them: defining the learning problem, combining bottom-up patient-level and top-down population forecasts, using machine learning, integrating heterogeneous data sources, and presenting results through an interactive, transparent interface. Coverage is hospitals and regions in England during the 2020 wave. The preprint is free to read and download on arXiv. Caveats: patient data are confidential and not released, forecast accuracy figures are not in the abstract, and the system was built for COVID-19 surge conditions. The authors conclude with lessons learned from one of the first machine learning systems deployed in hospitals at national scale during the pandemic. Simulation uses: an example of demand forecasting for hospital capacity planning and emergency response during a pandemic surge. Related records: CHIME (model-chime) and CDC FluSurge (model-cdc-flusurge) are simpler hospital surge models.
